public_rationale: Marcus says SpaceX will never match Amazon's roughly 2,538-fold return since its IPO. There is no deadline. SpaceX went public on June 12, 2026, at $135 a share, with a market value of about $2 trillion. Nothing by the evaluation date approaches a thousands-fold return, so the claim has not been proved wrong. A 'never' forecast cannot be confirmed early, so it stays open.
limitations: Price moves after the debut were not checked in detail. They matter only if they approach an Amazon-like multiple.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: SpaceX stock will never deliver returns comparable to Amazon's since its IPO.

statement.excerpt: Certainly, SpaceX will never return the way Amazon did.
statement.document_title: An entire industry is being propped up by math that is insane.

from_speaker: Certainly, SpaceX will never return the way Amazon did
Amazon returned 2,538x the original investment (earlier in the post)
our_interpretation: Read as a 'never' forecast: SpaceX stock will never deliver a return from its IPO comparable to Amazon's roughly 2,538-fold return since its 1997 IPO.
'Comparable' means a gain of a similar order: thousands of times the IPO price, split-adjusted.
criteria.support_condition: No deadline is stated, so this cannot be confirmed early. It holds for as long as SpaceX's return from its IPO stays far below Amazon's roughly 2,538x.
criteria.contradiction_condition: SpaceX's split-adjusted return from its IPO reaches a level comparable to Amazon's roughly 2,538x.
